question: In the processing and presentation of peptides of extracellular origin intervene (n):
analysis: In the processing and presentation of peptides of extracellular origin, the TAP proteins play a crucial role in transporting peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum for loading onto MHC class I molecules. The proteasome is involved in the generation of these peptides by degrading intracellular proteins. HLA-B molecules are MHC class I molecules that present peptides to CD8+ T cells. Tapasins are not directly involved in this process. HLA-DM molecules are involved in the peptide loading of MHC class II molecules, which present peptides derived from extracellular sources to CD4+ T cells.
